CLOUD REVIEWER seat for PR #2834 of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, at head 313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df. Bus nonce: 3b27b4f155360fea63cd8ff657184778. Never send push notifications. Write no Claude Code footer, no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer and no claude.ai session link in any commit, pull-request body or comment you produce; check your commits with `git log --format=%B` before pushing.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md and its rules from main, and follow them exactly. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin 313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df`; the PR body is in the PR. Verify each claim adversarially: mutate the fix and check the tests fail, and check every figure in the body at this head. Check that it merges with origin/main (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) and read CI on this head from the check-runs API.
Output: in a fresh directory of your own (`W=$(mktemp -d)`), write verdict.md, whose first line is exactly `Fix review: merge 313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df` or `Fix review: blocked 313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df <class>: <reason>` (no brackets; the class is lower-case letters and dashes), in the format the role file gives, then a blank line, then `bus-nonce: 3b27b4f155360fea63cd8ff657184778`, then the body in sections. A blocked verdict's block goes under `## Block`. Each finding this PR does not settle (a defect, a surviving mutant, a deferral, a follow-up, a task owed after the merge) is its own bullet under `## Findings` ending in its own `Carry: <GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>` (finding-propagation.md). Everything else (RESULT lines, re-runs, CI state, figures you could not re-derive) goes under `## Evidence`: tools/audit/carry_audit.py reads no item there as a finding unless it hands something on (deferred, for a later, follow-up, minor, advisory, residual, still has to, not blocking ...; a check that does not block is evidence only in the clause saying it is not a required check and does not block, never in the rest of its sentence: a nit or defect beside it is a finding), and the merge train parks a verdict holding a finding with no `Carry:`. Put the evidence files in `ev/` beside it, and make at least one file under `ev/` contain the full 40-hex head `313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df` (e.g. `ev/HEAD.txt` holding the head you reviewed, beside your command output): bus.sh refuses a verdict whose `ev/` names no head. Do NOT run bus.sh: its dispatch record lives on the orchestrator's machine, which publishes the verdict there (cloud_relay.sh). Return the verdict on a probe ref, and push nothing else; this builds one parentless commit with a private index and touches no branch of your checkout: `R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); G=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); mkdir -p $W/pr && cp -r $W/verdict.md $W/ev $W/pr/ && cd $W/pr && T=$(GIT_DIR=$G GIT_INDEX_FILE=$W/idx GIT_WORK_TREE=$W/pr sh -c 'git add -A -f . && git write-tree') && C=$(GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=seat -c user.email=seat@users.noreply.github.com commit-tree $T -m "verdict 2834 313a19d9189f7bbd87bcfbfe8dc231b8dbb4d3df") && git -C $R push -q origin $C:refs/heads/probe/rev-2834-3b27b4f1`. That ref is the return signal. Do not post comments, approve or merge.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Review of R10-ADVISOR-RESIDUE (first review of the fixer's handoff). The fixer's prompt was rendered WITHOUT this group's roster carries (cloud_dispatch --group omitted them; proposal V61), so the dominant risk is a carry the fixer never saw.

CARRY CHECK, item by item (mandatory): for EVERY numbered carry in the list below, state in your verdict evidence whether the diff and PR body satisfy it, with the file/line or the reason it does not apply. A carry that is neither satisfied nor shown not to apply is a BLOCKED verdict (class carry-missing), naming the carry index.

Review adversarially per dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md from a detached worktree at the head SHA, with the finder harness, never the fixer's. Say merge or blocked in fix-review.md grammar. No host or home paths in anything you push; cite repo-relative paths only.

=== CARRY LIST (roster carries 9 plus P141; the file is w34/carries-R10-ADVISOR-RESIDUE.p141.md; number them as listed) ===
Residue of #2257 that R10-ADVISOR (#2572, merged f24895c) recorded and left: its body's open seams (a) the what-if's single-solve monthly_cost_delta that the fuse advisor and the Advisor's 'Try in what-if' read, (b) the inbox sensor-gap and hot-water rows that scale one day to a month and swing, (c) the held estimator's per-solve asymmetry; and its reviews' notes: mutant MX4 (a pooled mean in price_tiles.published) survives because tests/features.py folds exactly two samples into every day, the degree tile prices a degree held while the plan delivers -0.514 K / +0.327 K per degree of setting (roughly 1.8x and 3x overstated), and a 30-day mean mixes days priced at different schedules. Each carry holds its source and evidence (routing audit 1). Fix MX4 with a fixture of unequal daily counts, decide the per-degree copy with the owner's screenshot as the finder harness, and size (a)-(c) with the null arm of r10_sav_null_terms.py before any change; a seam that does not move under its own perturbation is recorded, not fixed. Last group on #2257: closes it.

After: 

Carries (from the roster at 23b0a4cb; every one binds you):

[0] From #2572 (body, item a47745dc), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination #2257 is done and did not implement it (#2257 is open and no live group lists it; coordinator.py:8809 and :11242 still publish the single-solve `monthly_cost_delta` as the advisor's `cost_delta_sek_month`). **Open seam (a), the Plan page's what-if.** `async_simulate`'s `monthly_cost_delta`, which is also the fuse advisor's `cost_delta_sek_month`, scales the plan's single-solve spend, one-off coast or heat-up included. That is #2257 item 8's class, at the seam this group's architect note leaves alone. Its size is the `null` arm's `first_solve_plan` against `truth_per_delivered_degree`. The Advisor's "Try in what-if" lands on it, and `docs/dashboard-card.md` says so.

[1] From #2572 (body, item 69e7c431), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination #2257 is done and did not implement it (#2257 open, no live owner; seam (b) untouched after #2572 (no later commit names it: `git log --grep '#2257'` shows only 5e1fdb77b)). **Open seam (b), the inbox's sensor-gap and hot-water rows.** They are today's window, scaled to a month (the class seams above), so they swing day to day: #2257 item 6's class, outside the what-if this group owns.

[2] From #2572 (body, item 87849118), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination #2257 is done and did not implement it (#2257 open, no live owner; seam (c) was measured only in a scratch probe). **Open seam (c), the held estimator's per-solve asymmetry** between a degree cooler and a degree warmer. Its causes are the horizon's unsettled end state and the 15-minute quantisation of a coast. - Size: up to 23.5 of about 66 per month at one 07:00 start, in this seat's scratch probe (not a committed instrument). It averages to the `rotation` gaps above. - It is what keeps the brief's convexity check from being built here. A later change that wants that check, or compares the two tiles, starts from it.

[3] From #2572 (review 6322582323, item ae0472c3), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination R10-ADVISOR is done and did not implement it (MX4 still survives: tests/features.py:33575-33584 folds exactly two samples into every day, so a pooled mean equals the mean of daily means). **MX4 survives.** Replacing the mean of daily means with a pooled mean (`sum(sums)/sum(counts)`) passes features.py, because the horizon check folds exactly two samples into every day, so the two estimators agree. The check named `… publishes the mean of their daily means` cannot tell them apart.

[4] From #2572 (review 6322582323, item e8626144), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination R10-ADVISOR is done and did not implement it (the copy question (per degree held vs per degree of setting) was left to judge/owner; no later commit). **The null bounds the held figure per delivered degree, but the tile is read per degree of setting.** In the `null` arm the plan delivers −0.514 K and +0.327 K per degree of schedule moved, at +59.4 per delivered degree. Over a three-day loop, moving the setting a degree therefore changes the bill by roughly 30 and 19 SEK a month, against the tile's 54.4. The body states the delivered fraction, so this is disclosed. Whether three days reaches steady state is not shown.

[5] From #2572 (review 6328189370, item f1c7e1de), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination #2257 is done and did not implement it (same as ae0472c3 (MX4), round 2). Non-blocking: MX4 still survives at this head. I replaced the mean of daily means in `price_tiles.published` with a pooled mean (`sum(sums)/sum(counts)`), and `tests/features.py` reads `ALL 4282 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0 (`ev/mut-MX4.diff`, `ev/MX4-features.log`). The horizon check still cannot tell the two estimators apart, because every day it builds holds the same sample count. The body's "mean of their daily means" is not pinned against a pooled mean. A check needs days with unequal counts.

[6] From #2572 (review 6328189370, item 5df8a03b), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): its destination #2257 is done and did not implement it (same as e8626144, round 2). Non-blocking: the tile prices a degree held (+54.4 in the `null` arm). The plan delivers only −0.514 K and +0.327 K per degree of setting, so the row overstates what pressing the button saves, by roughly 1.8× and 3×. The body discloses this and leaves the copy question to the judge or owner. Nothing in this round changes it.

[7] From #2572 (review 6322344533, item 5f30f170), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): it carried no Carry: marker and is not implemented (same as e8626144). **Null control (carry 1).** The held figure reads +54.4 against +59.4 realised per delivered degree (−8.4 %, inside the fixer's own 15 % bound). But the plan delivers only −0.514 K / +0.327 K per degree of setting, so the tile overstates what moving the setting saves by roughly 1.8× and 3×. The body discloses this. Whether "a degree cooler ≈ 54" is the right copy for a button that moves the setting is a question for the judge or owner, not a block here.

[8] From #2572 (review 6322344533, item 4468b8a1), routed by routing audit 1 (2026-10-24): it carried no Carry: marker and is not implemented (the mixing question was left to the re-cut and not measured). **Mixing.** The 30-day mean mixes days priced at different schedules (after a target change, or an away setback that shifts `comfort_temp_day`). The overrides kept on the tile are only the latest. Not measured; stated so the re-cut can decide.

[9] (P141, triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch27.md#P141 at c9d4b1c2a; not on the roster at 23b0a4cb, so the running fixer never saw it) Move `_plan_slots` out of `coordinator.py`. It is a `@staticmethod` (`coordinator.py:4304-4305`) that collapses a per-step power schedule into `PlanSlot` dicts (`payload.py:626`) and reads no coordinator state. Its callers are lines 4477, 4485, 11234 and 11242. Put it beside `PlanSlot` in `payload.py`, or in a small plan-view module if `tools/audit/archscore/` reads that as sounder, and keep the call sites' behaviour byte-identical. Source: R10-ARCH-SHAPES #2819 round 2 added a second heating mask and moved archscore `coord_footprint` 2436 -> 2437 against round 1 (2446 at the merge base); moving the function out is the payment, routed here because a follow-on on ARCH-SHAPES would hold R10-HEAT-METER (critical path) behind it. Controls: archscore `coord_footprint` before and after, with its null control (a whitespace-only move of the same function inside `coordinator.py` does not move the metric); the published `slots` lists of the fixture captures (`coordinator.py:4541`, the space plan, and `4558`, the hot-water plan) are byte-identical before and after; one mutant that drops `shared_kwh` from the moved function fails the capture comparison.
